- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward surprise.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to forecast direction.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment volatility >0.5 in 3 consecutive days triggers “sentiment shock” correction: reduce forecast by 3–7% if sentiment turns negative, or increase by 3–7% if sentiment turns positive.
